--------
Order No. 02/ dated 13.09.2024 Heard learned counsel for the applicant and the learned Spl. P.P.
for the State.

2.  This bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant-Premchand Mahto @ Premchand Kumar Mahto with the prayer to release on bail in connection with Rajrappa P.S. Case No. 85 of 2024, registered under Sections 376, 313 of the Indian Penal Code, pending in the Court of the learned S.D.J.M., Ramgarh.
3. The F.I.R. of this case was lodged by the victim herself wherein the allegations are made that her husband had died on 19.01.2023.
She for the first time saw Premchand Mahto in village Bandiya at the house of her relative (Fua).
He took the mobile phone number of her and began to talk with her.
On 12.05.2023 he came to her house.
At that time, she was alone he raped her.
Thereafter he assured her that he would marry with her.
He also began to maintain her.
For one year continuous sexual is established between the two.
She also became pregnant.
She apprised Premchand Mahto in regard to the same.
He told that soon he would marry with her.
On 15.12.2023 the pregnancy was terminated by administering with some medication.
On 04.5.2024 she came to her parental village Siru thereto he established physical relation with her.
On asking by her to marry, he flatly refused and also hurling abuse assaulted her.
Hence this F.I.R. was lodged.
4. The statement of victim was also recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. in which victim has stated that on 12.05.2023 she was alone at her house.
Family members were out of the house and she was talking with Premchand over the mobile phone.
She told him that she was alone at the house.
He came to her house and established physical relation with her forcibly.

sentences.text: In October 2023 he took her to the Hotel Park Ranchi and thereto physical relation established.
On 11.04.2024 he also came to her parental house thereto physical relation established.
On 12.04.2023 again took to the hotel thereto established physical relation.

On 16.04.2024 he came to her house and also established relation with her and on refusal to marry she lodged the F.I.R.
5.

From the very perusal of the statement of victim under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. it is found that for the first time when physical relation was established by the petitioner with the victim on her saying that she would lodge F.I.R. he assured to marry with her.
But without getting married with the petitioner victim continued in courtship of petitioner.
She many times accompanied the petitioner in a hotel and resided there and established physical relation.
The thorough conduct of the petitioner shows that she was consenting party and the victim was already major and widow.
She knew the consequences of establishing physical relation without getting married.
6. In view of the above, the bail petition of the petitioner is hereby allowed.

Let the applicant be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the court concerned in the aforesaid case.
